title: #broadway #musicaltheatre #tonyawards #theoutsiders #review #theatre ...
transcript: I saw The Outsiders a couple months ago but I never posted about it and then I don't know it won some big award or something and now suddenly I feel like posting my thoughts so anyway I'm doing it now when people ask me what I thought of The Outsiders my go-to line has been that “it's a good show with some very good moments” but I also had some issues with it and I'm gonna talk about my criticisms but like just to be clear I don't think it's a bad show the book is pretty cohesive the music is pretty good the lyrics I think get better as they go along I'm not really a fan of the like exposition dumping in the first couple numbers but that problem definitely goes away as the show goes on I think the bigger issue for me is that I wasn't always a fan of where they chose to put the songs like there were songs that should have been scenes scenes that should have been songs but I also wanted more integration of like musical scenes and musical sequences there are a few moments like that like “Run Run Brother” or “justice for Tulsa” but I wanted more like that throughout the rest of the show one of the more egregious examples of this for me was in the big climactic confrontation scene in Act 2 between Dally and the brother where I just felt like screaming like “this should have been a song!” and then that scene is immediately followed by another song where we kind of grind to a halt for a tender character moment and I'm not opposed to tender character moments in fact individually I think most of them are quite good and I also wanna be clear that not every big emotional scene has to be a song in fact I often appreciate musicals that are willing to let their spoken scenes breathe and carry emotional weight and not just like fill in the gaps between songs But in this case I just think the balance was off something in the calibration was off and it just messed with the pacing. my other big thing might be kind of controversial which is that the Tony Award winning direction by Danya Taymor didn't totally land for me but I wanna give plenty of credit where it's due there is a lot that I like about what she contributed to the production especially in terms of the visuals and just the kinetics of the show the way she blended together the production elements and the movement that fight scene is pretty astounding it's like the best part of the show but as far as the tone and the actor direction I feel like it was trying to be kind of gritty and I just never really bought it there was too much of the like standard slick Broadway musical energy and some of it honestly just came across a little cartoonish to me but in other moments it feels like heightened melodrama and those actually tended to work for me and this kind of goes back to what I was saying about how I wanted more of the plot to be conveyed through song and I wonder if this show would have worked better for me as more of like a folk opera type format cause I think the show is actually at its best when it's using the music to lean into these grand operatic Dramatic with a capital D emotions
